title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: usage-based billing models in the model selector
summary: The licensing, access prerequisites, control paths and rollout statements are supported. Two dashboard descriptions need qualification: the comparison article still describes a credits-only, potentially point-in-time view, while the updated monitoring article documents local-currency cost estimates and distinguishes live dashboards from snapshot exports.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: General Availability is targeted for December CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: Preview is targeted for November CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "November CY2026"

claims.quote: "clouds": [ "Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Desktop and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": [ "Desktop", "Web" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": [ "General Availability", "Preview" ]

claims.claim: MC1519122 gives Frontier (Public) rollout from early November 2026 to expected completion by mid-November 2026.
claims.quote: Frontier (Public): Beginning early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption and the cost is variable, metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: UBB experiences consume Copilot Credits and require a USL for access.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users need a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license in addition to UBB.
claims.quote: Verify that users have a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL).

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: UBB must be enabled for users to access the announced models.
claims.quote: Enable UBB for users who should have access to the models.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Administrators must provide credits for users who should access the models.
claims.quote: Allocate credits to users who should have access to the models.

claims.claim: The USL provides a fixed-price foundation for everyday AI.
claims.quote: The USL covers everyday AI work, providing a fixed-price AI foundation for your workforce.

claims.claim: UBB covers advanced AI and frontier models beyond everyday AI included in the USL.
claims.quote: UBB is used for advanced AI and frontier models, extending beyond the everyday AI included in the USL.

claims.claim: Existing model choices are covered by the subscription.
claims.quote: Model selection is also part of the USL, with some models included with fair use, such as GPT 5.6 and Sonnet, and others included with limits, such as Opus.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Variable; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Interactions with UBB models consume Copilot Credits rather than being covered solely by a flat user fee.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing means charges are based on the work performed rather than a flat per-user fee.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has not published the Copilot Chat credit rates for GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com "GPT-6 Astra" "Claude Fable 5.1" credits rates model selector. Read USL/UBB, billing setup and billing comparison pages; results concerned availability, Cowork or unrelated Foundry/Databricks pricing, not Chat credit rates.

claims.claim: Administrators must set up a billing policy before users can use AI experiences requiring UBB.
claims.quote: Admins must set up a billing policy before a user can use AI experiences that require usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Spending policies are configured in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. 2. Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies is a documented Graph endpoint.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies?$filter=status eq microsoft.graph.spendingPolicyStatus'enabled'&$orderby=createdDateTime desc&$top=2&$count=true

claims.claim: The listed Graph call reads spending policies rather than configuring limits or alerts.
claims.quote: Get a list of spendingPolicy objects.

claims.claim: The beta APIs are subject to change and unsupported in production.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cost Management supports identity-based spending policies.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Identity-based policies scope access by users or groups.
claims.quote: Use this option when you need to manage usage by users or groups for a supported service.

claims.claim: Spending policies define access and limits rather than reserving or allocating credits to users or groups.
claims.quote: Spending policies only define access and spending limits, not credit allocation.

claims.claim: Moving between Entra ID groups makes the new group's spending policy effective for the user.
claims.quote: If a user moves from one Microsoft Entra ID group to another during a billing period, the new group's spending policy becomes effective for the user.

claims.claim: A user's consumption history carries forward across group and policy changes.
claims.quote: Credits consumed under the previous spending policy remain part of the user's consumption history and are accounted for when enforcing the spending limit under the new policy.

claims.claim: Credits are funded through billing methods including pay-as-you-go, P3 and prepaid capacity packs.
claims.quote: Organizations can access credits through capacity packs, Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans, or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go bills eligible usage to the linked Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go bills eligible Copilot Credit usage to the linked Azure subscription without an upfront credit commitment.

claims.claim: Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plans provide commit units over a one-year term.
claims.quote: Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans provide discounted commit units for eligible Copilot Credit usage during a one-year term.

claims.claim: P3 commit units are discounted.
claims.quote: They provide discounted commit units for eligible Copilot Credit usage during the plan term.

claims.claim: Usage beyond P3 credits can be billed as pay-as-you-go when enabled.
claims.quote: Usage beyond available pre-purchased credits can be billed as pay-as-you-go if pay-as-you-go is enabled.

claims.claim: Existing prepaid capacity packs can support services in this billing experience.
claims.quote: If you purchased capacity packs, you can use them with the services in this experience.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Administrators can set monthly policy spending limits.
claims.quote: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: Administrators can set monthly per-user credit limits.
claims.quote: Select monthly budget limits for users (optional). Use the toggle to select this option and to set a monthly limit for users to prevent a single person from spending all available credits.

claims.claim: Configured threshold alerts warn about consumption.
claims.quote: Select the administrators or stakeholders who must receive email notifications when policy usage reaches the threshold.

claims.claim: Users hitting the spending limit lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: A running task exceeding a per-user limit in a group policy can complete uninterrupted.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.claim: Global and Billing administrators can add, select and change billing methods.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.claim: The setup page says AI and License administrators can edit policies and manage limits and alerts.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods.

claims.claim: AI and License administrators cannot create spending policies according to the setup page.
claims.quote: However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: The same setup page inconsistently includes License Administrator among its read-only roles.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports. These roles provide read-only access to consumption information

claims.claim: Supported reader roles can view consumption information.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.

claims.claim: The access-request control is in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > All Settings > Access to usage-based billing experiences.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Settings > All Settings. 3. Select Access to usage-based billing experiences.

claims.claim: Configuring access requests requires the Global administrator role.
claims.quote: To configure the setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center, you need to be assigned to the Global administrator role.

claims.claim: Access-request setting changes can take up to 24 hours.
claims.quote: Changes to this setting might take up to 24 hours to apply.

claims.claim: The access-request selection does not complete UBB setup.
claims.quote: Your selection controls who can request access. It does not complete the usage-based billing setup by itself.

claims.claim: No users in the access-request setting disables requests, not model visibility or existing UBB access.
claims.quote: No users: Users cannot request a spending policy. Instead, they'll be presented with a link to learn more about Advanced AI experiences that require usage-based billing.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the access-request audience setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com graph powershell "Access to usage-based billing experiences" request spending policy settings API. Read access-request page and Graph Cost Management overview search excerpts; they document request handling, not this audience setting.

claims.claim: The Claude opt-in path is Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Anthropic > Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences.
claims.quote: On the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors page, under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Anthropic, and Save. 4. Under Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences, select your users or groups and Save.

claims.claim: The Claude opt-in requires AI Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a member of the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role to perform this task.

claims.claim: The Anthropic provider setting governs Claude models, not GPT-6 Astra.
claims.quote: When access is limited by user or group membership, only the assigned users can use Copilot features or agents that rely on that AI provider.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the Microsoft 365 Anthropic subprocessor audience setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com graph powershell "Anthropic" "subprocessor" settings API. Read returned Anthropic setup and opt-in excerpts and the full subprocessor and apps articles; no Graph or PowerShell operation for this setting was documented.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Claude models in Microsoft Copilot are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary

claims.claim: Claude models are also currently excluded from applicable in-country processing commitments.
claims.quote: currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.claim: Microsoft Product Terms and the DPA apply to Claude subprocessor use except models labeled with Data Retention.
claims.quote: Unless models are labeled "Anthropic models with Data Retention," the Microsoft Product Terms and Microsoft Data Protection Addendum (DPA) apply

claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention are off by default.
claims.quote: Anthropic models with Data Retention (such as Fable 5.0) have additional controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center and are off by default for all scenarios

claims.claim: Models with Data Retention require a separate tenant administrator opt-in.
claims.quote: No users will have access to these models until the tenant admin explicitly opts in to enable use of Anthropic models with Data Retention.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Anthropic's own terms apply to models with Data Retention.
claims.quote: Anthropic acts as an independent processor and use of Anthropic models with Data Retention is subject to acceptance of Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service and Anthropic's Data Protection Addendum.

claims.claim: Fable-class model terms can vary, including eligibility-dependent subprocessor availability for Fable 5.1.
claims.quote: Depending on your organization's eligibility, some Fable-class models may be available to your organization with Anthropic acting as a subprocessor.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls: credit requests
claims.claim: Credit requests are reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Overview > Top Actions > View requests.
claims.quote: From the Top Actions section, you can View requests and Manage spending policies

claims.claim: The documentation does not state whether the planned model-selector credit requests reach the existing Credit requests page.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com Copilot Chat UBB model selector hide disabled government cloud per-model limits credit requests. Read monitoring, USL/UBB and access-request articles and MC1519122; none links the planned selector requests to that page.

claims.claim: Requests unmatched by custom request policies continue through Microsoft's service and can be resolved in the admin center.
claims.quote: Requests that don't match a custom request policy continue through the Microsoft credit request service and can be resolved in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing discovery setting is deprecated.
claims.quote: The AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing setting is deprecated.

claims.claim: The deprecated discovery setting controls visibility.
claims.quote: The AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing setting controls whether users in your organization can see AI experiences that rely on usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Cost Management controls UBB access and spending.
claims.quote: this setting controls visibility, while Cost Management under the Copilot node in the Microsoft 365 admin center controls access and spending.

claims.claim: Dashboard totals are expressed in credits, not currency.
claims.quote: Everything in this view is expressed in Copilot Credits, not currency.
claims.fix: Replace 'expressed in credits, not currency; finance needs a translation to spend' with 'described as credits-only in the comparison article, but the monitoring article now also documents estimated cost in local currency, including negotiated rates; those estimates might not match the bill'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending alongside the comparison article.

claims.claim: Dashboard totals are point-in-time views.
claims.quote: Dashboard totals and exports might be point-in-time views and can refresh at different intervals.
claims.fix: Replace 'Dashboard totals are point-in-time' with 'The comparison article says dashboard totals and exports may be point-in-time views, while the monitoring article distinguishes point-in-time exported reports from dashboard views that continue retrieving live data'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management shows linked-subscription pay-as-you-go charges and P3 purchase or amortized costs.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges and purchase or amortized cost information for Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans (P3) and Microsoft Agent pre-purchase plans (P3).

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management does not show consumption against prepaid capacity packs.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management doesn't show consumption against Prepaid Capacity packs.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity-pack usage is monitored in the Microsoft 365 or Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Use the Microsoft 365 admin center or Power Platform admin center, as applicable, to monitor Prepaid Capacity Pack credit usage.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The selector presentation or hiding of metered models for users without UBB and credits is not established.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com Copilot Chat UBB model selector hide disabled government cloud per-model limits credit requests. Read discovery, access-request and USL/UBB articles and MC1519122; access gating is stated, but that selector presentation is not.

claims.claim: Government-cloud dates for this specific rollout are not published.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com Copilot Chat UBB model selector hide disabled government cloud per-model limits credit requests. Read roadmap, MC1519122 and government availability search excerpts; none gives government dates for this selector rollout.

claims.claim: Support for per-model spending limits in this Chat feature remains an open question.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com Copilot Chat UBB model selector hide disabled government cloud per-model limits credit requests. Read billing setup and management: policy and user limits are documented; model templates apply only to Cowork, not this Chat feature.

claims.claim: Users will be able to access UBB models through Chat's model selector.
claims.quote: Users will be able to access models that require usage-based billing (UBB) from the model selector in Chat.

claims.claim: The roadmap says tenant administrators need to allocate credits for model interactions.
claims.quote: Tenant admins will need to allocate credits so that users can interact with these models.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans requests to tenant administrators after users consume allotted credits.
claims.quote: If users consume their allotted credits, they will be able to request credits from their tenant admins.

claims.claim: MC1519122 names GPT-6 Astra as a generally available UBB model with the rollout.
claims.quote: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 will be generally available as UBB models with this rollout.

claims.claim: MC1519122 names Claude Fable 5.1 as a generally available UBB model with the rollout.
claims.quote: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 will be generally available as UBB models with this rollout.

claims.claim: The previously communicated eligibility requirements still apply to the announced models.
claims.quote: Previously communicated eligibility requirements for these models apply.

claims.claim: The notice also covers model-selector access in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
claims.quote: These models will be available from Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app and when using Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

claims.claim: Users will be able to set reasoning effort when using a UBB model in Chat.
claims.quote: Additionally, users will be able to set the reasoning effort level when using a UBB model in Chat.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: In-product requests for additional credits are planned after the initial rollout.
claims.quote: After the initial rollout, we plan to roll out the ability for users to request additional credits from their tenant admin.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions: credit requests
claims.claim: MC1519122 gives no date for the later credit-request rollout.
claims.quote: We plan to rollout the ability for users to request credits from their tenant admins after this initial rollout.

claims.claim: A spending policy can automatically apply to future supported services when that setting is enabled.
claims.quote: When a spending policy has Auto-apply new services turned on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy as they become available.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls: credit requests
claims.claim: View requests opens the documented Credit requests page for administrator review.
claims.quote: To view and approve credit requests from end users, select View requests. The Credit requests page displays all pending and approved requests.
